## Learning objectives

By the end of this activity, students will be able to:

1. Derive the intrinsic camera parameters that matter for mapping (pixel size, focal length in pixels, crop factor, angular resolution).
2. Compute image scale, Ground Sampling Distance (GSD) and ground footprint for a given flying height.
3. Design a block of images by choosing forward (*p*) and side (*q*) overlaps, and compute base and strip spacing.
4. Compare cameras of different formats (from smartphone sensors to large-format aerial cameras) at the same flying height and justify the choice for a given survey.

## What the worksheet contains

- **Parameters** — camera, ground coverage and resolving power, each with its formula and live value.
- **Angles & footprint** — field angles (approximate and exact), a 3×3 overlap diagram and the camera–height–footprint geometry.
- **All formulas** — a single table with every relation and its current numerical value.
- **Camera comparison** — 16 presets (UAV, DSLR, medium and large format, thermal) compared at the same height.
- **3D view** — an animated isometric view of the drone, image frustum and footprints.

## Suggested activity

1. Select the *1″ DJI Phantom* preset and find the flying height giving a GSD of 2 cm.
2. At that height, set *p* = 80 % and *q* = 70 %: compute base and strip spacing, and estimate the number of images for a 500 × 300 m area.
3. Switch to the *Phase One iXM-RS150F*: at which height do you obtain the same GSD? Discuss the consequences on footprint, number of images and flight time.
4. Compare the approximate and exact field angles: from which focal length does the difference become relevant?

## For instructors

- Works well live in class: change one input at a time and ask students to predict the effect before revealing it.
- Common mistakes: mixing mm and m in the scale denominator; confusing linear and areal scale; applying the overlap to the wrong side of the footprint.
- Extension: link the base-to-height ratio to the expected height precision (σ<sub>Z</sub> ≈ GSD · H/B).
